fact: An open cluster in Canis Major, about 2,300 light-years away and four degrees south of Sirius.
bio: Giovanni Battista Hodierna recorded it before 1654. About 100 stars belong to it, including several red giants and white dwarfs, and it is roughly 190 to 200 million years old. It spans about 25 light-years. In binoculars it forms a triangle with Sirius and Nu2 Canis Majoris, and it is sometimes called the Little Beehive Cluster.
